title: Measuring Semantic Deviation: Operationalizations, Experiments, and Falsification Conditions for a Theory of Meaning as Field Deformation
creator: Nobel Glas
description:
A research-program paper operationalizing the Semantic Deviation Principle for external replication. It specifies two executable regimes—closed-system deviation in a frozen language model and prospective retrieval-response deviation across public AI surfaces—and describes citation-graph deviation as a slower third regime.

The paper derives signed per-token deviation as a tractable local proxy, proposes a falsifiable human-versus-AI text comparison, and designs a Direct Preference Optimization experiment using deviation-derived preference pairs. Six anti-Goodhart protections, frozen models and datasets, statistical procedures, pre-registration requirements, and a twelve-month budget of approximately $14,000–$19,000 are specified. The record defines experiments and predictions; it does not report their execution or results.

wiki_article:
*Measuring Semantic Deviation* is Nobel Glas’s externally formatted empirical program for testing the Semantic Deviation Principle.

The heteronym note is methodological: Nobel Glas marks a measurement register intended to be independently replicable without requiring participation in the wider archive’s symbolic or institutional architecture.

Three operationalizations are presented.
